title: Jabber/XMPP: 25 Years of Digital Independence
summary: A reflection on XMPP (Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol), the open federated messaging standard that has operated for 25 years as an alternative to proprietary chat platforms. The article discusses how XMPP's decentralized architecture enables true digital independence and interoperability, though it has struggled with mainstream adoption compared to closed ecosystems like WhatsApp and iMessage.
problem_solved: Enables decentralized, interoperable instant messaging without depending on any single company's platform or server infrastructure.
why_valuable: Demonstrates that open, federated communication protocols can provide privacy-respecting, vendor-neutral alternatives to centralized messaging services that have dominated the market.
